source.paper: Wdowik, Varade, Vejpravova, Legut 2025, 'Magneto-Raman effect in van der Waals layered two-dimensional CrSBr antiferromagnet', arXiv:2503.15298 (v1)
source.locator: Fig. 5 and p. 5 discussion; Fig. 9 discussion (p. 6); Summary

items.text: At 4 K flake B shows additional features absent at 300 K (an Ag2 low-frequency shoulder near 220 cm-1 and a peak near 355 cm-1 next to Ag3), while flake A shows no such extra peaks at 4 K
items.locator: p. 5, Fig. 5: extra modes 'appear only in the 1L to 6L layers of CrSBr, and they are absent in the bulk system'

items.text: Concludes flake B is few-layer (paper: 1 to 6 layers) and flake A is thick / bulk-like, because the magnetic-order-related extra modes below TN are reported only for few-layer CrSBr
items.locator: p. 5; Summary: 'additional phonon peaks emerging below the Neel temperature ... only for 1-6 layers of CrSBr, but they are absent in its bulk form'

items.text: Links the extra low-temperature features to magnetic ordering below TN (about 116 to 132 K) and spin-phonon coupling
Notes that Ag2 (and Ag3) sit at slightly lower frequency in flake B than in flake A at 4 K, consistent with the redshift with decreasing layer number
items.locator: p. 6, Fig. 9 discussion: 'redshift of the Ag2 and Ag3 phonon frequencies with a decreasing number of layers'; p. 4, Fig. 3

items.text: In both flakes Ag2 and Ag3 shift to higher frequency on cooling from 300 K to 4 K
items.locator: p. 5 and Summary: above TN the Raman shifts decrease with increasing temperature; Fig. 5

items.text: Absolute intensities and baselines are not comparable between the two flakes (different thickness, optical interference, different export processing), so thickness should not be judged from intensity
items.locator: textbook: thin-film interference changes Raman intensity with thickness and substrate (Yoon et al. 2009, Phys. Rev. B 80, 125422); dataset: 6L traces background subtracted, 70L traces raw counts

items.text: Asks for an AFM thickness of both flakes, or for intermediate temperatures around TN, to confirm

wrong_claims.text: Claims flake A (the thick flake) shows the low-temperature extra modes
Concludes flake A is the thinner flake

notes: Label map (answer key): flake A = bulk (>70L, Figure5-70L.txt), flake B = 6L (Figure5-6L.txt), both from the paper's Fig. 5 (crossed +/- circular). The 6L traces are background subtracted in the dataset, the 70L traces are raw counts on a baseline near 2000; the context says only that processing differs. The 80 K and 150 K columns are left out to keep the case a two-temperature contrast.
